title: routing-bloom-signatures-for-decision-provenance
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Problem: Routing decisions (region selection, tier routing, fallback model variants) create multi-hop provenance that is expensive to store and query at high QPS. Current per-hop verbose traces increase storage and ingestion costs and slow live query/aggregation. We need a compact, queryable per-request signature that preserves set-membership of key attributes across hops to enable fast provenance checks, provenance-based sampling, and lightweight RCA without capturing full payloads.
proposed_design: Introduce a per-request Bloom signature: an evolving compact (128-512 bit) Bloom filter encoded as a base64 string attached to routing decision logs and traces. Each hop folds canonicalized routing attributes (region, tier, model_variant, policy_tags, decision_reason_token) into the Bloom signature using deterministic hash seeds. The signature is appended to existing decision events and stored as an indexed field in the routing telemetry index. Key features: incremental fold semantics so downstream hops can add attributes, merge semantics for parallel fanout, deterministic canonicalization rules to avoid false negatives, and tunable size/entry limits per deployment tier.
tradeoffs_and_risks: Pros: drastic reduction in per-request provenance size, O(1) membership checks for attribute presence, cheap aggregation queries. Cons: probabilistic false positives (configurable by size), not suitable as a sole source for legal auditing (supplement with sampled full artifacts), requires coordinated canonicalization across services to avoid mis-hits, adds minimal CPU cost to encode/decode at high QPS.
rollout_plan: 1) RFC and API contract: publish Bloom signature field name and canonicalization rules. 2) Pilot in staging: 1% of requests with full payload capture + Bloom signature to measure FP rate and storage savings. 3) Gradual rollout: 5% -> 25% -> 100% for non-compliance safe paths; keep full-capture sampling toggled. 4) Expose query helpers in Console and telemetry APIs for membership checks and 'where-did-this-attr-appear' views. 5) Post-rollout: monitor FP tail and adjust sizes/policies.
acceptance_criteria: Bloom signature appended to decision events in staging and searchable via Kibana/trace-store
Measured false positive rate < 0.5% for canonical attribute sets at 256-bit size in pilot workloads
End-to-end CPU overhead < 1% p99 for encoding at standard request payload sizes
Console query helper surfaces membership checks and returns links to sampled full artifacts when available
No regression in existing SLO dashboards or alerting during 25% ramp
tasks: Define canonicalization spec for routing attributes and decision_reason_token
Implement Bloom filter library and efficient base64 wire encoding in routing sidecar
Attach and propagate signature in decision event envelope and trace spans
Index signature field in telemetry store and add membership query support
Create sampling harness to compare Bloom membership vs full artifacts for FP measurement
Console UX: add 'Provenance Signature' tab and membership query tool
Run staged pilot and collect metrics, adjust params
